core_obligations: Remove the derived tensor product (proof lines 12412-12415): since the complex is a bounded above complex of flat modules, E^bullet tensor_O F equals E^bullet tensor^L_O F for every O-module F.

Use the tor amplitude hypothesis (proof lines 12416-12422): for every O-module F the sequence E^{a-2} tensor F -> E^{a-1} tensor F -> E^a tensor F is exact in the middle, because the middle-degree cohomology of the derived tensor product vanishes in degree a - 1.

Identify the Tor group (proof lines 12422-12427): the displayed sequence E^{a-2} -> E^{a-1} -> E^a -> Coker(d^{a-1}) -> 0 is a flat resolution of the cokernel, so the middle exactness says exactly that Tor_1^O(Coker(d^{a-1}), F) = 0 for all O-modules F.
Conclude flatness (proof lines 12427-12428): by the same-chapter Tor criterion the vanishing of Tor_1 against every module means that Coker(d^{a-1}) is flat.
proof_roadmap: Flat terms make the tensor product compute the derived tensor product.
The tor amplitude hypothesis kills the middle cohomology in degree a - 1 for every test module.
That middle cohomology computes Tor_1 of the cokernel.
The Tor criterion for flatness then applies.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a bounded above complex of flat modules with tor amplitude in [a, b], the cokernel of the differential d^{a-1} is again flat (statement lines 12402-12409). The proof has to align the degree bookkeeping: flatness of the terms makes the ordinary tensor product compute the derived one, the tor amplitude hypothesis is used in degree a - 1 to get middle exactness of E^{a-2} tensor F -> E^{a-1} tensor F -> E^a tensor F for every test module F, and the truncated complex E^{a-2} -> E^{a-1} -> E^a -> Coker(d^{a-1}) -> 0 is recognised as a flat resolution, which identifies that middle exactness with the vanishing of Tor_1 of the cokernel (proof lines 12412-12427). The final step is the same-chapter Tor criterion for flatness. The claim is H2: one degree-shifted bookkeeping argument, all inside the counted span.
